Slice 5 of [Release 2: implementation](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/101).

## Goal
After close, only the Lead sees the Result until they share it or the Review window ends.

## Acceptance criteria
- Pulse setting "Review window" 0–7 days, default 3, in the Pulse editor; 0 keeps R1 behaviour (share at once).
- Round states: Ready during the window, Shared after. The Lead's "Share with the team" moves it at once; the object's alarm shares it when the window ends. The Lead cannot extend or withhold beyond it.
- Members during the window: "Your Lead is reviewing these Results. They'll be shared by {date}." No scores, themes, or Note.
- Results-ready email: to the Lead at close, to members at share.
- Never waits for themes.

## Tests
- Lifecycle tests: window 0, manual share, automatic share, alarm runs twice.
- API privacy test: no Result data reaches a member before Shared.

## Follows
GLOSSARY: Review window, ADR 0006

## Context

Planned on the [Wayfinder map](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/85). Use `GLOSSARY.md` terms throughout. ADRs are in `docs/adr/`; research in `docs/research/`.
## Destination

Release 2 "Insight" (SPEC.md §8) is ready to build: comment themes, the discussion guide, the team health overview with Action markers, delayed sharing, the member's private history page, and German. Every decision that blocks R2 is recorded in ADRs (`docs/adr/`) and `GLOSSARY.md`, and R2 is split into implementation-sized issues under a "Release 2: implementation" tracking issue. R2 also carries the first real Round with the product owner's own team, which SPEC §8 placed after R1 (decision on #34, 2026-11-10).

## Notes

- Domain: as for Release 1 (map #1). `SPEC.md` is the source, `GLOSSARY.md` the vocabulary, ADRs 0001–0014 bind. Use glossary terms in every ticket.
- Planning only. No production code. Throwaway spikes are allowed as `prototype` or `task` tickets when a decision depends on one.
- **AI provider (product owner, 2026-11-10):** comment processing uses OpenRouter with the model `meta/muse-ember` (https://openrouter.ai/meta/muse-ember). This replaces SPEC §10 question 4's default (Workers AI only, through AI Gateway, prompt logging off) and needs an ADR. Known so far: served only by Meta, $0.10/M input and $0.50/M output tokens, not available through OpenRouter's EU in-region routing; zero-data-retention availability and structured-output support are not stated on the model page.
- SPEC §10 question 1 (raw comments or only themes for members) is still the R1 behaviour: members see no comments, the Lead sees redacted raw comments behind N (ADR 0001, 0009). R2 tickets decide what themes change.
- Grilling tickets: call the Skill tool for `grilling` and `domain-modeling`. Research tickets: call `research`. Record hard-to-reverse decisions as ADRs.
- Trust before features (SPEC §3.1): when a choice trades anonymity for convenience, anonymity wins. Anything sent to a third party is a new data flow and must be stated plainly to members.

## Decisions so far

- [What is in and out of Release 2?](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/86): Themes at Round close behind N (Lead keeps raw redacted comments, members see themes only); redaction stays rule-based; AI opt-in per Organization and disclosed to members; discussion guide by rules plus optional AI, Lead only; overview is one Team over time with Action markers; delayed sharing is a Lead review with automatic sharing after 3 days; history page shows participation from the server and answers only from the member's browser; German for app, answer page, and emails, per Person; no R1 deferrals; the first real Round starts early in R2.
- [Can OpenRouter with meta/muse-ember process comments within SurveyBeat's privacy rules?](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/87): No: Meta, its only host, keeps prompts 30 days in the US. ADR 0015: `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` through OpenRouter with `provider.zdr: true`, pinned to `google-vertex/europe` and `amazon-bedrock/eu-west-1`, no fallback, only redacted text sent, about $0.0015 per Round, off by default per Organization.
- [What are comment themes, who sees them, and how do they keep anonymity?](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/88): ADR 0016. Computed once at close behind N; at most 5; each needs 2+ comments; no quotes (6-word-run check); members see label and sentence, the Lead also counts and raw redacted comments; no Lead edits; retry up to 24 h.
- [What does delayed sharing delay, and for whom?](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/89): Review window 0–7 days per Pulse (default 3); the Lead shares or it shares automatically; members see a "being reviewed" notice; results-ready email at share.
- [How can a member see their own history without linking them to their anonymous Submissions?](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/90): ADR 0017. Participation from the server, own answers only from the browser (1 year, clearable), shown next to shared Team scores above N.

- [How is German added to the app, the answer page, and emails?](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/93): ADR 0018. Typed per-locale catalogs, Person → browser → Organization language, per-locale prerendered answer pages, informal du, bilingual Template, language never stored with a Submission.
- [What is the discussion guide, and is it generated?](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/92): ADR 0019. AI-written in the same call as themes, behind N with AI on; four sections, at most 3 questions; same no-quote check; no fallback; Lead only, not editable; the Lead writes a Note the Team sees.

129-**Discussion guide**:
# The Organization Durable Object owns each Round's state and schedule, and Release 1 uses no Workflows

SPEC §6.2 suggests a Workflow per Round plus an hourly Cron job that creates Rounds. Instead, each Round's state, together with a schedule table of its due jobs (open, send for a time zone, remind, close, compute, notify, create the next Round), lives in the Organization's Durable Object. One DO alarm is always set to the earliest due job, and the alarm handler runs each job as an idempotent DO method in the same transaction as the state change it makes. A daily Cron job only wakes every Organization's DO to repair a missing alarm.

This keeps one owner and one store for each Round. With Workflows, step results would be persisted outside the DO, a Workflow-to-DO bridge would have to be built for Effect, and every transition would span two systems that can each run a step twice. The cost is a small scheduling loop of our own on top of the alarm's at-least-once retries.

## Consequences

- A local time becomes UTC when its job is scheduled, using IANA time zones. Send times are restricted to 06:00–21:00 local.
- Exactly-once sending is enforced on the Invitation row (`pending → sending → sent | failed(reason)`, with a lease). A lease that expires with no outcome becomes `failed: unknown` and is shown to the Lead with Resend, never resent automatically. So a crash can cause a visible gap but never a duplicate.
- Workflows remain an option for later long-running jobs, such as AI theme generation in Release 2, if a DO alarm is a poor fit.

I built and merged #106 (PR #127). Every CI check passed, including e2e and the preview privacy check. I did not try the flow by hand on the deployed stage.

1. **States and transitions:** close moves the Round to Ready and fixes the window's end on the Round. Leads get the results-ready email at close. The Round becomes Shared when the Lead clicks "Share with the team" (Lead only, admins are refused) or when a new `share` job runs at the window's end. Members get their email at share. Window 0 shares straight away, as in R1. Both paths go through one share step that only changes a Ready Round, so a doubled click or alarm does nothing. Themes are never awaited.
2. **Deviations, all for privacy:**
   - Sharing a Round also shares any earlier Ready Round of the same Pulse, because the later Round's trends already contain its scores.
   - The Note from #105 is hidden from members on the server until Shared.
   - The migration is `0015` (`0014` was taken by Notes).
   - Members still see Submission counts and response rate during the window, as they do while a Round is Open.
   - Existing Pulses get the default of 3 days.
3. **Rebase fixes:** a few test fixtures from #104/#105 assumed a member sees themes or the Note on a just-closed Round. I changed them to Shared Rounds.
4. **Reviewer findings:** backend had no defects. I added the two missing tests it named (the earlier-Ready-Round case, close early with a window) and fixed one gap myself: a member made Lead during the window would have missed their email. On the web side I fixed a brief flash of the member notice for Leads. I left the cosmetic items, including a share button that re-enables for a moment before the page reloads.
5. **Not fixed (existed before this change):** if computing a Round's Result fails three times, the Round stays Closed and its window never starts.
6. **Tests:** 847 unit, 125 privacy, 14 workerd (Organization + Notes), covering window 0, manual share clicked twice, automatic share with the job run twice, and the Note.
7. **Merge:** squash commit `c3637558f4b6da82b890cee3b71f557f86dd0676`. The remote branch is deleted; the local one stays because this worktree has it checked out.
